statements.t: “With KT-621 and KT-579, we are advancing complementary immunoregulatory mechanisms that target distinct drivers of disease, with significant potential to address unmet needs across the current treatment landscape.
The last patient has now completed their week 16 visit in our KT-621 BROADEN2 Phase 2b atopic dermatitis trial, and we plan to report topline data by year-end 2026.

The results provide an important foundation as we advance KT-579, our 7 th degrader to enter the clinic, toward a study in lupus patients and explore the opportunity for targeting IRF5 in additional autoimmune diseases.

Beyond these clinical programs, our research engine remains focused on unlocking novel biology and pursuing high value targets to build the next wave of oral medicines for patients who need effective, safe and convenient treatment options.”
The Company plans to report topline data by year-end 2026.
Subject to discussions with regulators, the Company expects to initiate the first Phase 3 trial in AD by mid-2027.

Leveraging its unique target selection strategy, proven small molecule discovery capabilities, and deep development expertise, the Company continues to advance an early pipeline of novel oral programs with a goal to deliver at least one new development candidate per year.
The Company does not expect to recognize additional collaboration revenue in 2026.
Kymera expects that its cash balance will provide the Company with a cash runway into 2029 beyond multiple clinical inflection points in its pipeline.
A live webcast of the event will be available under News and Events in the Investors section of the Company’s website at www.kymeratx.com .
